verdict: Major revision required. curriculum_v2 repairs the factual-QA coverage, source-quality coverage, c25.2 containment, internal synthesis, and overstrong top-level prerequisite findings from review_v1. It does not repair the research-design boundary, and it introduces or preserves blocking mutual-confidence defects in c25.1.2, c25.1.6, and c25.1.7. The available held-out evaluations cover only applied QA, so the source-grounded, verification, and tutoring branches remain evaluation-insufficient rather than validated.
blocking_findings: Boundary remains unresolved between c25 and c25.1.5. c25 excludes "Original empirical research or execution of experiments," while c25.1.5 includes "Bounded experimental designs for specified hypotheses" and its representative asks for a controlled labeling-and-trapping experiment. c25-d03 is an exact counterexample: designing a new stereochemical, isotope-labeling, kinetic, or trapping experiment to distinguish Prins and ene mechanisms is both an included bounded design and original empirical research design. Separating execution from design does not define when a novel design ceases to be excluded original research.

Mutual self-confidence fails in c25.1.6. Its entry tests a commonly taught fact, but its outcome and includes combine dated factual recall, definitions, specialist principles, and short applications across varied domains. Mastering eval-11, recall of a 2017 global vaccination percentage, does not predict success on c25-d14, recall and application of UCC §2-207, or c25-d07, recall of specialist fermentation regulation. The mixed-domain representative hides the failure by concatenating unrelated items rather than establishing transfer between bodies of knowledge. The review_v1 knowledge-regime problem has been relocated from c25.1.1-c25.1.4 into one broad catch-all leaf.

Mutual self-confidence fails in c25.1.2. c25-d10 requires a direct 28%-7% difference, whereas eval-08 requires combinatorial instruction scheduling under dependency, latency, register-preservation, and resource constraints. Both are admitted as quantitative relation or constraint calculations, but success on the former does not predict the sequencing and search operation central to the latter. Constraint scheduling should not be grouped with direct relation application merely because both return a number.

Mutual self-confidence remains implausible in c25.1.7. c25-d12 requires Taylor-style small-angle linearization and order counting, while c25-d15 requires first-order quantum perturbation theory and a parity argument. These use distinct mathematical operations and specialist models; mastery of either does not predict the other merely because both simplify a model. The split from c25.1.2 repairs the direct-calculation versus modeling contrast but leaves c25.1.7 internally composite.
mutual_confidence_findings: c25.1.6 counterexample: eval-11's dated-statistic recall versus c25-d14's specialist legal-rule application changes both the body of knowledge and the operation. The section also mixes the broadly expected knowledge regime in its entry with specialist closed-book recall in its includes.
c25.1.2 counterexample: c25-d10's one-step subtraction versus eval-08's resource-constrained dependency scheduling. Their shared numerical answer form does not supply a shared central operation.

c25.1.7 counterexample: c25-d12's asymptotic linearization versus c25-d15's parity-based perturbation calculation. Both are model simplifications, but the techniques and prerequisite knowledge do not transfer reliably.

No comparable structural counterexample appears in the probes for c25.1.1, c25.1.3, c25.1.4, c25.1.5, c25.2.1, c25.2.2, c25.2.3, c25.3.1, c25.3.2, c25.3.3, c25.4.1, or c25.4.2: each keeps its central operation stable and generally supplies the governing content. This is only design evidence; there are no direct held-out evaluations for most of these leaves, so their empirical mutual confidence is insufficiently evidenced rather than established.
continuity_findings: Valid edge c25.1.2 <- c25.1.1: the dependent representative must select the stated timing, dependency, and resource rules before combining calculations; the entry adds one substitution after selecting the governing relation and quantities.

Valid edge c25.1.3 <- c25.1.1: the representative selects relevant parts of a supplied regulatory model before tracing them; the entry adds one downstream causal step after selecting the affected link.

Valid edge c25.1.4 <- c25.1.1: the representative must select definitions, thresholds, priority rules, and exceptions from supplied material; the entry adds application of one exception to the selected baseline rule.
Valid edge c25.1.5 <- c25.1.3: the representative must trace both supplied mechanisms to their predicted observations; the entry adds selection of the measurement that separates those predictions.
Valid edge c25.1.7 <- c25.1.2: the representative first selects and combines governing quantitative relations; the entry adds one stated approximation and identification of the negligible term.

Valid edge c25.2.1 <- c25.1.1: the representative retains relevance selection while extending it to similar records with entity, date, and condition distractors; the entry adds paraphrase-based location in a document.
Valid edge c25.2.2 <- c25.2.1: the representative retrieves provisions and case facts from several documents before joining them; the entry adds one cross-passage entity join to two retrieved facts.

Valid edge c25.2.3 <- c25.2.1: the representative locates the statements relevant to one disputed date before assessing their sources; the entry adds one provenance-weighting judgment after retrieving the direct answers.

Valid edge c25.3.1 <- c25.2.1: the representative retrieves a passage for every atomic claim with the correct entity, date, quantity, and scope; the entry adds supported/contradicted/not-established classification to targeted retrieval.

Valid edge c25.3.2 <- c25.1.2: the representative audits a multi-step calculation, so quantitative-relation mastery is used in full; the entry adds error localization rather than a new calculation family.

Valid edge c25.3.2 <- c25.1.3: the representative audits a supplied failure mechanism through its consequential steps, so mechanistic tracing is necessary; the entry adds identification of the first invalid inference.
Valid edge c25.3.2 <- c25.1.4: the representative checks a conditional safety rule and its exception, so supplied-rule application is necessary; the entry adds audit and immediate-effect analysis.
Valid edge c25.3.3 <- c25.3.1: the representative decomposes the disputed claim and classifies each evidence relation; the entry adds combination of those classifications into a provisional verdict.
Valid edge c25.3.3 <- c25.2.3: the representative weighs expertise, recency, scope, provenance, and independence; the entry adds a claim-focused verdict to those source-quality judgments.
Valid edge c25.4.2 <- c25.4.1: the representative must construct a transparent worked correction from the supplied solution; the entry adds targeted adaptation for one stated misconception.

The invalid review_v1 edges c25.3 <- c25.1, c25.3 <- c25.2, c25.4 <- c25.1, and c25.4.1 <- c25.1 were removed. No v2 prerequisite edge repeats their requirement that a dependent master an entire sibling branch whose full outcome is unused.
other_findings: Prior blocking-finding recheck: closed-book factual QA is now structurally covered by c25.1.6; provenance and source-quality checking are covered by c25.2.3 and c25.3.3; c25.2 now permits one or more sources and contains c25.2.1; c25.1's representative now synthesizes one heat-treatment disposition rather than stapling unrelated deliverables; c25.1.1, c25.1.3, and c25.1.4 now use supplied knowledge; and the overstrong c25.3/c25.4 prerequisites were removed. The c25 versus c25.1.5 research boundary remains unresolved, while c25.1.6 preserves the prior knowledge-transfer problem in a new leaf.

Guidepost accounting: C25.1 maps to c25.1.6 for closed-book factual QA and c25.2.1 for provided-source retrieval; C25.2 maps to c25.2.2; C25.3 maps to c25.3.1 and c25.3.3, with c25.3.2 covering reasoning verification; C25.4 maps to c25.4.1 and c25.4.2. All four guideposts have structural homes.

Discovery accounting: c25-d01, c25-d02, c25-d04-c25-d09, c25-d13, c25-d14, and c25-d16 primarily map to c25.1.6 because their governing specialist knowledge is not supplied; c25-d03 maps to c25.1.5 but exposes the c25 boundary contradiction; c25-d10 maps to c25.1.2; c25-d12 and c25-d15 map to c25.1.7. c25-d11 is underdetermined because its required list of candidate quadrilaterals is absent and therefore does not count as positive evidence. Thus 15 discovery tasks are placeable and one is malformed; none directly supports c25.2, c25.3, or c25.4.

Held-out evaluation accounting: all four C25 probes concern c25.1. eval-07 and eval-11 map to c25.1.6; eval-08 maps to c25.1.2; eval-10 maps to c25.1.6 rather than c25.1.4 because the hypothesis-testing rule is recalled rather than supplied. There are no applicable held-out probes for c25.2, c25.3, or c25.4, so source-grounded QA, verification, and tutoring have insufficient evaluation evidence.

Internal-node synthesis is repaired. c25 uses one learner safety dispute across answering, retrieval, verification, correction, and explanation; c25.1 uses one heat-treatment failure and one disposition decision across all seven children; c25.2 uses one eligibility decision and one document packet; c25.3 uses one public-safety explainer and verdict; c25.4 uses one learner solution and misconception. None of these representatives is merely a concatenation of unrelated child deliverables.

Every section has one entry and one representative instruction, and the representatives differ substantively from their entries. Apart from the blocking c25.1.6 mixed-domain construction, the probes are instantiable and supply the facts, models, rules, records, or correct solutions needed for transformation-oriented outcomes.
